subject: TAM shift synchronization & coverage matrix — RFI response
messages:
From: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@midtownbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@midtownbank.com>, procurement@midtownbank.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: TAM coverage windows + escalation expectations

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. As part of our security & operations review, procurement asked us to provide more detail on your TAM (technical account manager) coverage model so they can evaluate 24/7 vs. business hours SLAs. Can you please provide the following in your RFI response: 

- Typical TAM-to-customer ratio for enterprise customers with reserved capacity
- On-call shift patterns (hours, timezone handoffs) — specifically how you ensure overlap during handoffs
- Escalation matrix (who gets paged at each severity level) and expected response times per severity
- Incident communications cadence (initial ack, updates cadence, postmortem timing)

If you can attach a sample coverage matrix and an example incident comms schedule that would be ideal. Our target for the procurement review is EOD Friday, 14 May.

Regards,
Lisa
Lisa Carter
Director, Cloud Procurement
Midtown Bank

P.S. copying Samir from SRE.
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@midtownbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFI: TAM coverage windows + escalation expectations

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a consolidated RFI appendix. High level answers below and attached a draft coverage matrix (redwood_tam_coverage_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a simple overlap diagram. Long answers follow in the attached sheet but summary here: 

- TAM ratio: For reserved-capacity enterprise customers we target 1 TAM per 8–12 active L2/L3 contacts (varies by throughput & contract tier). We staff dedicated TAM leads for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- On-call shifts: primary coverage is 08:00–20:00 local business hours (customer local tz) with a shared on-call for critical (P1) outside business hours. Handoffs include a 30–60 minute overlap window and a rolling weekly schedule to avoid burnout.
- Escalations: P1 -> on-call TAM & on-call SRE -> assigned engineering escalation (if no remediation in SLA window) -> Director on-call. Response targets: P1 ack within 15 min, P2 ack within 1 hour, P3 ack within 4 hours.
- Incident comms: initial acknowledgement within target ack time, status updates every 30 min for active P1s, hourly for P2s, daily for P3s until resolved. Postmortem published within 5 business days; RCA within 10 business days for Severity P1.

I'll loop in Vivek and Ben for the technical overlap and escalation contact list and to confirm the on-call paging tiers.

Attachments: redwood_tam_coverage_matrix_v1.xlsx, oncall-overlap-diagram.png

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Director, Customer Success (EMEA & US)
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@midtownbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFI: TAM coverage windows + escalation expectations

Hi all —

Following Monica's summary, a couple of technical clarifications from the SRE/ops side that procurement typically asks for: 

- Handoff specifics: we enforce a 45-minute overlap for any cross-timezone handoff that crosses more than 3 hours difference (e.g., US<>APAC). The outgoing on-call does a readout in the ticketing system (we use PagerDuty + Jira) with recent latency/cost anomalies and any active prefetched KV cache warmups.
- Paging: P1 pages PagerDuty -> SMS + mobile push to TAM + SRE primary; P2 uses email + PagerDuty low-noise push to TAM; P3 handled during business hours via email routing.
- Escalation ownership: we keep an explicit mapping in the coverage matrix linking customer-facing TAM -> SRE primary -> L3 engineering rotation. That mapping is versioned per contract.

Ben — can you confirm the phone escalation list (Director+VP numbers) and whether procurement needs a redacted sample of our on-call roster?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Reliability Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@midtownbank.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:38:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFI: TAM coverage windows + escalation expectations

Hi Lisa —

Attached is a redacted example of our on-call roster and the completed coverage matrix for Midtown. Key points / clarifications as requested by procurement: 

- Ratio & staffing: committed TAM lead + named backup; who-to-contact list included in matrix. For Dedicated customers with SLA-backed throughput we assign a 1:6 TAM ratio as part of the contract.
- Overlap pattern: we proposed a 45-minute overlap for handoffs crossing >3h diff; 30-minute overlap for same-region handoffs. Diagram attached.
- Escalation matrix & response times: included in the matrix table. For contractual SLAs we can move P1 ack to 10 minutes under a negotiated enterprise SLA.
- Incident comms cadence: initial ack -> 15 minutes (P1, negotiated) with 30 min updates; post-incident RCA deliverable timeline and distribution list included.

Action items: 
- Monica: finalize and sign off on the coverage matrix for Midtown by EOD Thu (13 May) so procurement can include it in the RFP bundle.
- Grace: please add the Director+VP on-call redacted numbers to the third tab of the sheet.

Thanks — attaching: redwood_tam_coverage_matrix_v1.xlsx, oncall-overlap-diagram.png

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Enterprise TAM
Redwood Inference

On behalf of Redwood — happy to set a 30-min call with your SREs if you want to walk the matrix live.
